$comment: Single-node readiness ledger for the hardware proof-of-concept.
This file is the CHECKED-IN, DIFFABLE record of what the cluster manifests
claim versus what one box can actually deliver. The auditor fails on DRIFT
away from this record: a new app-of-apps identity collision, a new workload
declaring redundancy it cannot have on nodeCount nodes, or a PVC total that
outgrows nodeDiskGib. Every acknowledgement below is DEBT with a reason and
STATUS: awaiting maintainer sign-off on nodeDiskGib (see below).
Dejan 2026-08-14 - drafted from a live single-node bring-up, not from a plan.
2026-08-21 - nodeDiskGib is NO LONGER the auditor's only comparator, because
it never was a measurement. The `capacity-provenance` check compares the same
declared totals against MEASURED hardware read off the checked-in ClusterNode
registrations under maintainers/*/cluster-nodes/*/node.yaml, and it REFUSES
(exits 1) when no registration carries a measurable spec.hardware.storage.
The nodeDiskGib budget line is still checked and is still useful as the
procurement target - it is simply now labelled ASPIRATIONAL in the output,
which is what it always was.
$comment_activeStorageProfile: Which rung of full-ai-cluster/k8s/storage-profiles.json THIS deployment runs.
REQUIRED - readLedger refuses a ledger without it, because a default rung
would let the storage-profile check report agreement with a profile nobody
selected, which is a check that cannot fail.
THE LADDER, and the box each rung needs. Longhorn never offers a node's raw
disk to replicas. The tree that owns this ladder leaves both reserve settings
at longhorn-1.7.2 chart defaults - storageOverProvisioningPercentage 100
(values.yaml:214) and storageMinimalAvailablePercentage 25 (:216) - so ~75%
of a disk is placeable, less the OS root:
minimal    200 GiB declared    172 GiB at bring-up   ~297 GiB box
standard   595 GiB declared    467 GiB at bring-up   ~823 GiB box
measured   967 GiB declared    467 GiB at bring-up   see the arithmetic below
large     1599 GiB declared   1099 GiB at bring-up  ~2162 GiB box
`measured` IS ACTIVE, and it is named for where its numbers come from: every
claim that provisions on a fresh sync gets `standard`'s capacity, and the
three claims that provision NOTHING keep `large`'s planning ceilings.
WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. All 17 cuts from `large` are SIZE cuts.
Not one pod count moves: cockroachdb keeps 3 Raft members, nats keeps a
3-node JetStream cluster, mimir keeps 3 ingesters and 3 store-gateways,
redis keeps 2 read replicas. `minimal` is the rung that trades quorum for
disk - it drops cockroachdb and nats to 1, which removes Raft quorum for
real - and that is exactly why `measured` rather than `minimal` is the rung
for this box: the disk is there, so no HA has to be sold to fit on it.
THE ARITHMETIC, against maintainers/Addisons820/cluster-nodes/node-ad1efd:
raw, every block device                        1047 GiB  <- what the gate compares
schedulable, 75% of (1047 - 30 GiB OS root)     763 GiB  <- what Longhorn will place
schedulable if only /dev/nvme0n1 is a Longhorn
disk (defaultDataPath: /var/lib/longhorn sits
on the root filesystem, so /dev/sda is not
one until somebody mounts and adds it)        676 GiB
measured, bring-up                              467 GiB  fits both, by 296 / 209 GiB
measured, declared                              967 GiB  under raw; OVER schedulable
THE LAST LINE IS A STANDING DECISION, NOT A PASSED CHECK, and the auditor
prints it on every run rather than leaving it buried here. The 500 GiB gap is
ollama (200), vllm (200) and the arc runner model cache (100): two
manual-sync Applications and one PVC manifest that no Application applies.
None provisions on a fresh sync, so the cluster comes up well inside the
schedulable bound - but syncing them at these ceilings would ask Longhorn for
storage it will refuse to place. They are left alone deliberately: shrinking
a ceiling nobody has decided to lower would buy headroom the bring-up total
never spends, and would quietly delete a capacity intent instead of costing
it. Running `standard` instead takes declared to 595 GiB and clears the
schedulable bound outright, at the price of those ceilings (ollama and vllm
200 -> 48, arc 100 -> 32). That is Aaron's call, and it now has its number.
$comment_nodeDiskGib: Usable disk per node, in GiB, dedicated to the replicated-storage class.
DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. Running the auditor prints the sum of every declared
PVC capacity x pod count. Re-measured 2026-08-21 after the shrink:
longhorn          967 GiB   (profile "measured", the checked number)
longhorn          911 GiB   (the extractor's independent reading; it
cannot see mimir's chart-default pod counts
and mis-attributes redis master's - kept as
a cross-check, not as the answer)
zeta-local-path   103 GiB   (the extractor's reading of our YAML - the same
cross-check status as the 911 above, NOT the
answer; see the paragraph below)
zeta-local-path   193 GiB   (the RENDER, 2026-08-22: 117 full-ai-cluster +
76 infra, from rendered-storage-claims
.snapshot.json. Trust this one.)
THE TWO zeta-local-path FIGURES DISAGREE BY 90 GiB AND BOTH ARE PRINTED, because
naming the better number is honest and quietly deleting the worse one is not.
103 is what the readiness extractor derives from our own YAML, and it is wrong
in BOTH directions, which is why it looked plausible for so long:
OVER   it counts full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications/platform/blueprints-flowdent
.yaml's 8Gi mssql `Blueprint`, which is a TEMPLATE - a PVC exists only
once a Deployable references it, and none does.
UNDER  it cannot see a claim that renders with NO storageClassName and
therefore BINDS this class as the cluster default: loki backend + write
(10 each), mimir-alertmanager (1), dapr scheduler (1). That is 22 GiB
today and was 30 until 2026-08-22, when hindsight's postgres (8) moved
onto the longhorn it had always claimed.
The extractor is NOT fixed here - reading a blank class as the cluster default is
a change to how it resolves every claim, and it is left as a named gap rather
than a silent one. The render is the measurement; this pair is the cross-check.
(this comment is a dated snapshot and has drifted twice already: 1499/73 on
2026-08-14, 1599/1409 on 2026-08-21 under profile `large`. The auditor prints
the live numbers; trust those over this paragraph.)
2048 IS NOW LOOSE RATHER THAN TIGHT, and that is the useful change. It was
chosen as the next standard NVMe size above a ~1.4 TiB reading and was
slightly UNDER what `large` needed. The active rung needs 967 GiB declared
and only 467 GiB at bring-up, so a 2 TiB node is no longer the requirement
the manifests imply - it is headroom. The open procurement question changed
shape with it: it is no longer "buy 2 TiB or the cluster cannot come up" (it
can, today, on the 1047 GiB node-ad1efd) but "how much of the deferred
model-cache ceiling do we want to be able to actually sync", which is 5.1 of
docs/design/2026-08-21-the-zeta-bootstrap-usb-full-design-document.md.
It is still NOT a measurement of any box, so it is still not what the auditor
VERIFIES against; that is the measured ClusterNode registrations. See
$comment_acknowledgedCapacityShortfall. It is kept, and kept labelled
ASPIRATIONAL in the output, because a procurement target that quietly
disappears once the cluster fits is a target nobody ever revisits.
Measured counter-example (2026-08-14, kind 0.31.0 on podman/applehv, one
node, 100 GB disk): the catalogue oversubscribed the disk ~15x. Longhorn
reported ReplicaSchedulingFailure 'insufficient storage;precheck new replica
failed', volumes went robustness=faulted, and cockroachdb-0/1/2 never left
Init:0/1 with AttachVolume.Attach failed 'volume is not ready for workloads'.
That is what an under-budgeted node looks like.
$comment_nodeCount: Nodes in the PoC cluster. One box today. Raise this as workers join; every
acknowledgedFalseRedundancy entry below should be re-examined when it does,
because most of them stop being false at nodeCount >= 3.
$comment_acknowledgedFalseRedundancy: Workloads that declare replicas > nodeCount WITHOUT hard anti-affinity, so
Kubernetes co-schedules every replica onto the one node. They come up green;
the redundancy is nominal and the failure domain is a single disk. Listing
one here does NOT make it safe - it makes it stated, so nobody demos it as
high availability.
full-ai-cluster/cockroachdb  3 Raft members, chart default podAntiAffinity
type=soft. Observed co-scheduled on one node.
full-ai-cluster/vault        server.ha.replicas=3 with raft.enabled=true.
Same shape: Raft quorum, one failure domain.
full-ai-cluster/nats         JetStream config.cluster.replicas=3. Same shape.
AND IT WAS NOT EVEN THAT until 2026-08-22: the
block sat at TOP LEVEL, where nats 1.2.7 never
read it, so the StatefulSet rendered replicas: 1
and this line acknowledged a nominal redundancy
that did not exist in either sense -- one pod,
no quorum, and any stream created with
replicas > 1 refusing outright. The block is
under `config:` now and the render was
re-measured, so the entry is true as written:
three co-scheduled pods on one disk.
full-ai-cluster/redis        replica.replicaCount=2. Async replication, so
no quorum to lose - but no redundancy either.
full-ai-cluster/platform     examples/gmod-server.yaml replicas=2. A sample
workload, not part of the PoC critical path.
full-ai-cluster/kubevirt     virt-operator Deployment replicas=2, from the
VENDORED upstream kubevirt-operator.yaml
(v1.8.4, line 8493). Upstream ships 2 for
control-plane HA; on one node both co-schedule.
NOT edited down to 1 on purpose: that manifest
is vendored byte-for-byte so it stays 1:1 with
what runs, and node-5b2dfa really does run two
virt-operator pods today. Editing it would make
the checked-in copy diverge from the cluster it
documents, which is a worse lie than this one.
Resolves at nodeCount >= 2 with no code change.
Removing an entry from this list is the fix, and the fix is one of: drop to
nodeCount replicas (honest single node), set hard anti-affinity (the shortfall
becomes visible Pending pods), or add nodes.
$comment_acknowledgedCapacityShortfall: EMPTY, and that is the point of this round. It carried
longhorn=1599GiB>>1047GiB@node-ad1efd
from 2026-08-21 until the manifests were shrunk to fit the measured box.
The debt is retired by ARITHMETIC, not by exemption: activeStorageProfile
moved from `large` (1599 GiB) to `measured` (967 GiB) and the manifests were
rewritten to match, so the declared total is now under the 1047 GiB measured
bound and there is no shortfall left to acknowledge. Nothing about the check
was relaxed - re-run the auditor and it does the same comparison it always
did, against the same measured evidence.
WHAT THIS KEY IS FOR, still. A capacity shortfall against MEASURED hardware
may be carried here as debt, recorded as
`<storageClass>=<declared>GiB>><measured>GiB@<node>`. The key carries BOTH
numbers on purpose: acknowledging the bare storage class would make the check
unfalsifiable, silently absorbing any later PVC growth or a smaller node
joining. Pinned, every movement of either side goes red and has to be
re-stated deliberately.
Provenance of the measured side: maintainers/Addisons820/cluster-nodes/
node-ad1efd/node.yaml, written by zeta-install.sh from
`lsblk -ndo NAME,SIZE,TYPE -e7` on that node during a real metal boot
(2026-06-09) and committed by a self-registration PR. lsblk's human sizes are
BINARY, so 931.5G is 931.5 GiB and compares directly to Kubernetes Gi.
The bound is deliberately GENEROUS: it counts /dev/sda, which is very
possibly the USB stick, and it reserves nothing for the ESP, the root
filesystem, swap, or Longhorn's own reserve. So exceeding it is proven
oversubscription and no reading of the hardware rescues it; NOT exceeding it
proves nothing on its own. The inference convicts, never acquits - which is
why the auditor now also PRINTS the schedulable estimate (~75% of disk less
the OS root, from the deployed Longhorn reserve settings) beside the raw
bound. That estimate is a report and not the gate, because it assumes which
block devices Longhorn manages and how big the OS root is, and a bound built
on assumptions can be wrong in the acquitting direction.
Two of the registered nodes (maximdolphin's node-f82aa6 and node-5b2dfa)
record NO hardware.storage at all - the post-boot self-register path never
captured it. They are excluded from the bound and printed as unmeasured
rather than counted as zero.
NOTE: the UNVERIFIED case is not acknowledgeable here and must not become so.
A shortfall you can see is debt; an absent comparator is an absent check, and
an exemption for it would be the vacuity this ledger exists to prevent.
$comment_acknowledgedRootAppDuplicates: argocd/zeta-root is declared TWICE with two different spec.source.path values:
Kubernetes has exactly one object at that identity. Both roots carry
prune: true + selfHeal: true, so whichever is applied last owns the name and
prunes the other tree's entire child Application graph.
This is the mechanical reason the two trees cannot both be pointed at one
cluster, and the reason 'run the live test against both trees' is not a
cheap option. Tracked for consolidation; delete this entry when one tree
